> 民之飢，以其上食稅之多，是以飢.

Chapter 74 was about who may kill. Chapter 75 answers where the not-fearing-death came from.

And the chapter's most loaded character is one we use every day without noticing.

## 治 is the name of a river

治: 水。出東萊曲城陽丘山，南入海.

治 is a river — the Zhi, flowing south into the sea.

From the river came 治水, water management. From water management came 治理, governance.

So 治 was water work from the beginning. Not the handling of people.

And water work has one rule everyone knows: you cannot block water, you can only channel it. Build the dike and the water rises; raise the dike and the water gets worse.

## 民之難治

Read with the character's history, this is an irony: why are the people hard to govern? Because you are 治-ing them — with the blocking method.

The Guodian and Mawangdui texts have 民之不治 for the received 民之難治. One character, two weights: 難治 is "difficult"; 不治 is "cannot be governed at all."

## 以其上之有為

What is 有為? It is building the dike.

The chapter's three clauses all have this shape — a symptom in the people, a cause in the one above:

- 民之飢，以其上食稅之多 — hungry because the tax taken is too much.
- 民之難治，以其上之有為 — ungovernable because he keeps building.
- 民之輕死，以其上求生之厚 — careless of death because he has piled his own life thick.

## 飢 is not 饑

The two characters were never confused by the ancients:

飢，餓也 — the belly is empty.
饑，穀不熟為饑 — the harvest failed.

飢 is man-made; 饑 is weather.

The chapter uses 飢. Laozi does not write 民之饑 — a famine year. He writes 民之飢 — empty bellies.

He leaves no room for the sky to be blamed.

## 求生之厚

Same 厚 as chapter 50's 生生之厚: the thickness of piling it up.

The one above piles his life thick, and the people become careless of theirs — because the cost of living has been transferred to them, and what has been taken cannot be defended by being careful.

## 賢 is a price, from 貝

賢: 多才也, from 貝 — the shell, the unit of value.

So 賢 carries price in it: worth counting, worth ranking.

夫唯無以生為者，是賢於貴生 — only the one who does not make a business of living is worth more than the one who prices life high.

The last character reverses into the first: 賢 (worth) is used to say that 貴生 (pricing life) is worth less.

## The chapter's structure

Three symptoms, three causes, one source: the one above has taken from below — grain, room, and life.

And the whole thing is expressed in the vocabulary of water works, because the remedy is the same as the diagnosis: you cannot stop a river by pressing on it. You can only give it a channel.

## A test

Take a system that has become "hard to manage" — a team, a household, a process. Ask what has been taken from the people in it: time, room, discretion. Then ask whether the difficulty is in them or in the dike.
